problem: The equation is not balanced. Left side has 4 Cl (TiCl4); right side has 3 (TiCl3) + 1 (Al(C2H5)2Cl) + 1 (C2H5Cl) = 5 Cl. Carbon and hydrogen balance, but chlorine does not, so the reduction step as written is impossible.
fix: Write the reduction without the extra chlorine: TiCl4 + Al(C2H5)3 → TiCl3(s) + Al(C2H5)2Cl + C2H5• (an ethyl radical, which is lost by side reactions). If a stable-molecule product is wanted, use the balanced overall form 2TiCl4 + 2Al(C2H5)3 → 2TiCl3(s) + 2Al(C2H5)2Cl + C2H4 + C2H6.

problem: "Atactic polypropene is not the product" is too absolute and clashes with the earlier "largely isotactic". Industrial Ziegler-Natta polypropene is typically about 90-95% isotactic and always carries a small atactic or low-tacticity fraction.
fix: Say: "The product is largely isotactic; a small atactic fraction usually forms too and is removed in the plant."

problem: Metallocenes are not part of the Ziegler-Natta family; they are a separate class of single-site catalysts that also work by coordination-insertion. Calling them "of this family" can make a student write metallocene as a Ziegler-Natta catalyst in an exam.
fix: Say: "Metallocene catalysts are soluble single-site catalysts that follow the same coordination-insertion mechanism but are not Ziegler-Natta catalysts; they give very uniform polymers."
